resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. writing §13 (value-prop / positioning framing; hard sub-rule: vendor in body is suspect) line 9: harm: The judge's facts check out, but its harm claim does not. I grepped the body (above <!-- maintainer -->) and found exactly two hits: L7 "evaluate the vendors" and L9 "vendor stories". L54 sits in the maintainer block. The phrase does echo the project value prop; compounded/2026-04-28-writing-value-prop-leaks-into-curriculum-body.md quotes it as "practitioner-grounded findings, not vendor stories". No accept-note in the maintainer block covers it.

The harm lens is where the finding fails.

(b) The harm is just the rule restated: "strategy-doc phrasing, and the rule bars it from a teaching beat." It names no effect on a reader. §13 exists to stop body prose defending the curriculum's own credibility ("not an aspirational vendor story", "this isn't marketing"), because that reads defensive and marketing-shaped. L9 defends nothing about the curriculum. It tells an engineering manager what happens in their own procurement: without hands-on competence, the only input left is what vendors pitch. That is the lesson this section exists to teach. The maintainer block places it as the strategy's "Three things NOT to do" (the platform-first move), taught on purpose.

(a) Nobody in the room is worse off. "Evaluate the vendors, choose the tool, roll it out" literally describes the tempting move. An EM recognises it as their own calendar, not as marketing.

(c) The fix costs more than the defect. "You end up choosing on guesses" drops the mechanism. The gap is filled by someone else's pitch, not by randomness, and that mechanism is what sets up the pull argument and the Fin contrast: a platform grown from what engineers built versus one picked from a pitch. "Guesses" is vaguer and slightly wrong, and it weakens the section's central claim to satisfy a keyword. The L7 swap to "compare the platforms" is harmless but buys nothing.

The rule's letter ("audit every body hit; usually swap") calls for an audit, not an automatic swap, and this hit passes the audit.
